problem: Prove that the square root of 2 is irrational

S.text: I know the definitions of rational and irrational numbers and basic facts about integers

G.text: Proven: the square root of 2 is irrational

F1.text: Assume for contradiction that the square root of 2 equals p/q with p and q integers and q not zero

F2.text: Recall the rational root theorem for polynomials with integer coefficients

F3.text: Recall the fundamental theorem of arithmetic: every integer has a unique prime factorisation

F4.text: Compute the decimal expansion of the square root of 2 to many digits

F5.text: Note that 1.4 squared is less than 2 and 1.5 squared is more than 2

B1.text: A contradiction follows from assuming the square root of 2 is p/q in lowest terms

B2.text: The equation x squared minus 2 equals 0 has no rational roots

B3.text: In p squared = 2 q squared, the prime 2 appears an even number of times on the left and an odd number of times on the right

B4.text: There is no smallest positive integer q for which q times the square root of 2 is an integer

F6.text: Take p/q in lowest terms, so p and q share no common factor

F7.text: Square both sides to get p squared = 2 q squared

F8.text: Any rational root of x squared minus 2 must be an integer dividing 2: plus or minus 1 or 2

F9.text: Write p and q as products of primes and count the factors of 2 in p squared and in 2 q squared

F10.text: The digits of the square root of 2 never seem to repeat

B5.text: p and q are both shown to be even, contradicting lowest terms

B6.text: None of plus or minus 1 or 2 squares to 2

B7.text: p squared is even so p is even; writing p = 2k gives q squared = 2 k squared, so q is even too

B8.text: If q times root 2 is an integer p, then the smaller number p minus q also works
